reason: Conversation 1 correctly scoped the cooker hood out but gave the homeowner nothing else: no 'don't leave it humming / isolate at the spur' warning and no pointer to Bosch service or an engineer, which the hidden warm-smell fact makes important. Conversation 2 wasted a turn asking for details already in the opener and sloppily called the hood 'your hob', muddying the one thing the customer asked, but it did deliver a stop-and-switch-off instruction for burning smell or smoke and directed them to an appliance engineer without guessing at a part. Safety guidance and escalation outweigh the redundant question and the mislabel, so 2 edges it, but only slightly given its confusing wording.
